what_it_does: Modern data centers send network traffic in two forms: traffic between servers within the same data center and traffic between different data centers (often geographically distant). These two types of traffic have very different characteristics—local traffic has millisecond delays while cross-data-center traffic can have hundreds-of-millisecond delays. Current networking systems handle these separately, which leads to unfairness where one traffic type crowds out the other. Uno is a unified system that controls congestion (network slowdowns) and prevents packet loss for both traffic types simultaneously using a single coordinated approach.
